patients.label: 42-year-old Malay man with multifocal lacunar infarctions and mild cognitive impairment
attribution_limitations: The text says the patient refused referral to a counsellor or psychiatrist while Table 2 says a counsellor or psychologist; each names two possible targets and they differ, so both refusals are kept literally and review-only.

The MoCA-paragraph statement that there was no feature suggesting depression and post-stroke dementia is recorded as absent findings at that assessment; it sits beside earlier low mood, frequent tearing and feelings of uselessness and a 'Yes' to the checklist mood item. These are different time points and are not treated as a conflict, and no depression diagnosis is recorded as present or absent.

The post-stroke checklist mood item asks about feeling more anxious or depressed and is answered Yes; which of the two applies is not stated, so it is review-only. Low mood is documented separately in the narrative.
The musculoskeletal pain diagnosis at the outpatient clinic is not stated to be wrong and its relation to the stroke is not stated; no refutation is recorded.

Neurological findings are normal with motor strength 5/5 at the health clinic assessment while left-sided hemiparesis was documented at the second episode; the encounters carry no dates, so these are kept as separate time points and not treated as a conflict.
The stroke date is printed as April 2022 in the abstract and 2022 in the case presentation; these are consistent and the more precise month is used.

limitations: The source has no figures, no supplementary material and no media; raw.xml contains no supplementary-material element.

Almost no event has a calendar date; only the stroke month (April 2022), the first-week interval to the second episode and the 6-week MoCA interval are timed, so most events are ordered only where the text states order.
The post-stroke checklist rows, Table 2 and the MoCA domain Table 3 are stated without per-item dates; Table 3 is general background.
The refused referral is a counsellor or psychiatrist in the text and a counsellor or psychologist in Table 2; both are review-only.
The post-stroke checklist mood item (anxious or depressed) is review-only because it joins two states.
The MoCA paragraph opens with 'Thereafter' after Table 1; as a paragraph-opening order word it is not used to order the MoCA after the specialist assessment.
